title: skills(ci): two-speed CI — fast set on PR and merge-queue runs, full battery hourly on main and before a release, main-red stops the lane, four required contexts plus the guard, timing gates report-only, test budgets not deletions
body:
Filing gate ③: a maintainer-directed governance card. Filed by the director seat (summon #37, `session_01LqNgdPZB2Jnr5HpGbaqLeB`) on the maintainer's words in this seat's session on 2026-10-12, verbatim: 「我觉得能让整个车队提速的方案就是好方案，main 很多天才会发一个版本，我只要确保发版本之前做好各种测试就可以。」 and, on the rules below as presented, 「同意，立卡」; then, on scope, 「然后 objectui cloud 仓库也要看一下，是否需要类似的方案。」 and 「cloud 仓库是私有项目， ci 要收钱，这个更要优化整体时间。」. ⛔ Not a claim. Reader: the `domain:skills` lane. Every file this card changes is a governed surface (Tier H): the PR stays a draft until the maintainer approves it.

## The doctrine, in four rules

1. **Two speeds.** A `pull_request` or `merge_group` run carries the FAST SET: gates and tests that read the change's own inputs, under a wall budget (10 minutes for the whole queue entry; each lint lane 5 minutes at median). `main`'s hourly `schedule` run and its `push` run carry the FULL BATTERY: every gate, every tier, every suite, the live-server and dogfood legs included. Nothing is deleted or weakened by this card; it moves.
2. **The release gate reads the full battery.** Before the `release` environment approval (ADR-0125), a job reads the newest full-battery runs of `CI` and `Lint & Type Check` (`schedule` or `push`) whose head is at or before the release commit, and the publish lane refuses when either is not `success`. "Tested before a release" is a gate, not a promise (ADR-0049's spirit).
3. **Main-red stops the lane.** A red on `main`'s full battery is the owning lane's first work: triage files it under the main-red convention, the lane's next PR carries the fix, and no PR of that lane arms the queue while its red stands. A gate that reds packages the PRs did not touch twice in an hour is flipped to report-only by any seat before any ruling (the timing-gate rules below).
4. **Required set of four, plus the guard.** The merge queue's required contexts become `Lint & Repo Gates` (an aggregator over lanes, name kept; #22991), `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (about one minute; it guards the Tier H contract and is kept for that reason, not for speed — the maintainer may strike it). `Dogfood Regression Gate` and `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` leave the required set and run in the full battery. AGENTS.md's required-set paragraph (`:519`) is rewritten to say so.

### Timing gates (from seat post #12708, block H)
- A measurement gate (suite-duration ceilings, shard timing drift, any gate that grades a duration) never reds a required job: it reports, through `continue-on-error: true` or a separate advisory check.
- A gate measures and judges on the same run profile: a ceiling learned from `schedule` runs is not enforced on loaded merge-group runners.
- A new exit-grading gate soaks report-only for at least a week of runs before it grades.
- Any seat flips a gate that reds untouched packages twice in an hour to report-only, before any ruling; the ruling follows.

### Tests: budgets, not deletions
- Each package's suite weight keeps a ceiling that only a ruling raises (`RULED_CEILING_RAISES`); the ceiling step reports (as ruled on #22949) and the report is read at the full battery.
- A slow test file is fixed, not deleted: a file over 10 s of wall is a card for the owning lane (the 29 s and 18 s files named in the 2026-10-12 queue reds are the first two).
- A test is deleted only with a named duplicate: the PR names the other test that pins the same assertion at a layer at least as close to the code. ⛔ No bulk deletion.
- Dogfood (254 files) and e2e (89 files) belong to the full battery, not to every PR; `Test Core` stays affected-only on PR and merge-group runs, as it is today.

## What this card changes (one PR, Tier H, draft until approved)
1. `AGENTS.md`: the required-set paragraph (`:519`) names the four contexts plus the guard; the two-speed doctrine and the main-red rule are written beside it; the timing-gate and test rules join the gates section, each citing this card.
2. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Console Pin Gate` and `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` run on `schedule` and `push: main` only (the jobs gain an `if:` on the event; the `on:` block is unchanged), so a PR and a merge-group run carry `Build Core`, `Test Core` and `Build Docs`.
3. `.github/workflows/release.yml`: the full-battery check of rule 2, before the environment approval.
4. Branch protection and merge-queue required contexts: the maintainer removes the two contexts from the required set after the PR lands (a repo-Settings act; no seat can). The card's landing record carries the before and after.
5. `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md` and `triage-duties.md`: the main-red rule and the flip-to-report-only rule.
6. **objectui and cloud follow the same doctrine.** The director seat measures both repositories next and files one sibling card per repository where the measurement warrants it. For cloud, a private repository whose runner minutes are billed, the budget is total runner-minutes per merged PR, not only wall time; objectstack and objectui are public, where GitHub-hosted standard runners are not billed.

The lint lanes themselves are #22991 (ruled D, 2026-10-12), this card's first execution. Named as follow-ups, not carried: `Type Check · workspace` (11.8 min median on merge groups, the next bottleneck; a build-and-typecheck of the whole workspace with the turbo cache saved on `main` only) and the `Test Core` shard variance (3.7 min median, 15.2 p90: runner load).

## Measured on 2026-10-12 (the director seat's reading; per-run data on #22991)

| leg, merge groups, 15 runs | median | p90 |
|---|---|---|
| `Lint & Repo Gates` | 14.0 min | 22.9 |
| `Type Check · workspace` | 11.8 | 12.8 |
| `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` | 8.2 | 8.6 |
| `Dogfood Regression Gate` (each of 6) | 6.8 | 8.3 |
| `Console Pin Gate` | 6.7 | 10.3 |
| `Dogfood Verify CLI` | 6.5 | 7.7 |
| `Build Docs` | 3.9 | 4.3 |
| `Test Core` (each of 6) | 3.7 | 15.2 |

A queue entry costs about 122 runner-minutes (`CI` 83 + `Lint & Type Check` 39). 498 PRs merged in the trailing 7 days. Test files 3,755 → 5,158 since 2026-09-18; the timing table's total weight 67 → 187 minutes since 2026-09-27 (part of that is a measurement change; the file count is not). For scale, the CircleCI 2025 State of Software Delivery report puts the industry's median workflow at 2 min 43 s, p75 near 8 min and p95 above 25 min, with a 10-minute benchmark.

Expected after this card and #22991: a PR's feedback in about 5–6 minutes and a queue entry in about 8, from 14–36 today.

## Acceptance
- A product-only PR's checks all conclude within 10 minutes on three consecutive merge-group entries; the moved jobs appear on the next hourly run of `main`.
- A deliberate red in a moved job (a dry run on a branch, never on `main`) is reported by the full battery and the release job refuses that commit.
- `AGENTS.md` and the two skill references carry the rules verbatim, citing this card.

Related: #22991 · #22949 · #19189 / #19686 · #22076 · #16496 · ADR-0125 · ADR-0049 · seat post #12708 (block H).
